summary: iter188 UX/growth — backend GET /api/referral/my-pending + driver sky-blue header + scheduled badge blink + client referral-progress nudge — ALL PASS. Backend pytest 3/3 (/app/backend/tests/test_iter188_ux.py). UI: referral-progress-banner appears for a referred client B (text 'Plus qu'une course pour débloquer vos 5EUR !', progress bar present) and clicking it navigates to /referral. A fresh client A with no pending referral does NOT see the banner (count=0, GET /referral/my-pending returns {pending:false}). Client home renders correctly (menu-btn, search-services-bar, nav-home) and the theme is orange (no sky-blue/green primary surface). Driver header (driver-menu-btn, online-toggle, scheduled-reservations-btn, notifications-btn) renders with background rgb(14,165,233) = #0EA5E9 — sky-blue confirmed. With a seeded scheduled pending taxi ride, scheduled-badge is present with text '1' and class includes 'animate-blink-turn'; the button has 'animate-blink-ring'. Clicking the calendar opens scheduled-sheet listing the reservation with an orange 'Accepter' button (bg rgb(255,80,0) = #FF5000). Notifications-badge also rendered (best-effort). No JS pageerrors. Audio playback cannot be asserted headlessly; code path /lib/driverAlert.js exists with unlockable AudioContext and is imported by DriverHome.js without throwing on page load.

integration_issues.flow: Driver active-ride overlay vs header buttons
integration_issues.issue: When driver has an active in-ride state (e.g. Jean Dupont demo with seeded ride), the in-ride sheet visually overlaps the sky-blue header at the top — header buttons are still present in DOM and clickable via JS, but a real user with a long in-ride sheet may not see/reach the scheduled-reservations-btn while in-ride. Not a regression from this batch (the same overlay existed before) — flagged for UX consideration.

critical_code_review_comments: UserHome.js fetch('/api/referral/my-pending') uses credentials:'include' but no Authorization header — relies on the access_token cookie set by /auth/login. Token-only clients (mobile SPA without cookie) would silently see no banner. Consider using the central apiClient with Bearer attachment, consistent with other fetches.

DriverHomeHeader.jsx scheduled-badge applies animate-blink-turn on the DIGIT and animate-blink-ring on the BUTTON — visual effect is strong, but ensure prefers-reduced-motion is respected in index.css (currently @keyframes blink-turn/blink-ring with no @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override). For accessibility consider disabling the animation when reduce-motion is requested.

driverAlert.js uses an unlockable AudioContext that requires a first user interaction — Safari iOS may still gate this even after touchend depending on context; recommend documenting that the siren may be silent on the very first incoming request after page load until any tap occurs.

Both badge and button apply the same animation name 'animate-blink-turn' on the digit; if React re-renders the badge frequently (every notif poll) the animation may restart mid-cycle and look choppy. Consider memoizing the badge subtree.

POST /api/rides validation rejects nested {pickup:{lat,lng}} objects and requires flat pickup_lat/pickup_lng — fine, but the public schema is undocumented for testing agents (had to seed mongo directly). Consider adding /api/rides/sample or example payload.
Notifications poll is best-effort; if the polling endpoint becomes 401/expired the badge will silently disappear — add a console.warn for monitoring.
